answer: Standing is a violet that only shows its true colors when an identity does diverse, verifiable work: each epoch’s work must differ in kind from the last — a different task, a different skill, a different proof — and a ferrous core of standing only forms when the colors keep changing, like a walnut that ripens only after many different seasons. A farm of a thousand fakes has only one color: each fake repeats the same cheap task, so its violet stays flat — and each fake must pay fresh effort for every new kind of work, with no bulk discount for repetition.
